title: Flood risk forces halt to rescues in Tibet, as Nepal death toll rises to 469 - The Guardian
description: Flood risk forces halt to rescues in Tibet, as Nepal death toll rises to 469  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
Rescuers searching for survivors of Wednesday’s deadly flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have been forced to pull back after a debris dam overflowed, increasing the risk of fresh flooding.

Residents in Nepal’s Rasuwa district, on the border with Tibet, were seen rushing up hillsides ⁠on Friday to escape a possible surge in the river, ⁠according to witnesses. Authorities in Nepal had stopped rescue operations for at least 90 minutes, an army officer said.

A lake formed after a wall of mud and debris struck the border hub of Gyirong in Tibet on Wednesday, causing catastrophic flash floods that thundered down valleys and obliterated villages.

The risk of ​the lake bursting had prompted Chinese rescue personnel and vehicles to withdraw to a safe area, the Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported on Friday.

Barrier lake forms at base of mountains near Nepal border

The confirmed death toll from the floods – which were triggered by the collapse of a glacier – rose on Friday to 469 in Nepal, with more than 1,300 people missing there and in Tibet. Five people have been so far confirmed dead by Chinese authorities.

More than 500 foreign citizens were among 826 people missing in Nepal, police and tourism ⁠officials said, including 177 from India, 90 from the US, 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada. Chinese state media said at least 558 were missing on the Tibet side of the border, of whom at least 260 were foreign nationals.

Climate crisis could be destabilising mountain areas like Nepal, experts warn Read more

The flood on Wednesday had destroyed power stations, roads and bridges along a route that links Kathmandu with Lhasa in Tibet and is ⁠popular with trekkers and pilgrims.

In its wake, debris had formed the barrier lake that was threatening further flooding. China mobilised an eight-member engineering team to conduct aerial surveys ​and 3D modelling of the lake on Thursday, and by Friday its reservoir had topped 2.5m cubic metres of water, up from the estimated 1.5-2 m cubic metres the engineering team recorded a day earlier.

Rescue efforts in Bidur, the capital of the Nukawot district in Bagmati province, Nepal, were disrupted on Friday morning as the the Trishuli River began to rise again after the lake near the China border burst its banks.

Rescue workers were moved from the area and residents who had tried to return to what remained of their homes were told to evacuate again immediately.

Bidur, once a bustling town on the banks of the Trishuli, now lies in ruins. Most homes were washed away when a tide of mud, rocks and debris surged down the river valley early on Wednesday. Survivors described clinging to buildings and trees as the water rushed over them.

The mangled concrete remains of a bank, a government office and an ATM booth were among the few structures left standing, although they were submerged in mud. Officials said there were still bodies inside the buildings but it was too dangerous to recover them.

Nearby, locals gathered along the muddy road, calling out for lost relatives and trying to dig out what was left of their belongings.

Most areas battered by flash floods remained accessible only by army helicopter. At the Bidur army camp, where much of the rescue effort was being coordinated, rescue and military helicopters flew in and out every five minutes, bringing in dozens of traumatised victims. Many said that in a matter of minutes, the floods had taken their loved ones, their homes and everything they owned.

The international community is scrambling to get aid to flood-stricken parts of Nepal and Tibet.

View image in fullscreen Sludge inundates homes after flash floods in Nuwakot district. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images

Nepal has said it does not yet need foreign assistance as the search-and-rescue operation – complicated by the destruction of dozens of bridges and miles of roads across the mountainous region – continues.

“The offer for help is natural,” Lok Bahadur Chhetri, a spokesperson for the foreign ministry, said on Friday. “Our security agencies ‌are doing the search and rescue operation. For now we don’t require such help.”

The Kathmandu Post reported that India, China, the US, Britain, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh had asked the government to allow their search-and-rescue teams to assist in the operation.

Dinesh Bhattarai, a former Nepali ⁠ambassador to the UN in Geneva, said the government’s reluctance to ​accept foreign assistance may ​be linked to sensitivities over ​Rasuwa district and its border with China’s Tibet region.

“They may have thought about ​the locational sensitivity ‌of the region and ​decided not to ​accept foreign teams,” Bhattarai told Reuters.

But Chhetri said Nepal’s own rescue teams were handling the operation and the decision to refuse foreign assistance had nothing to do with sensitivities involving China.

Scant information has emerged from Chinese authorities about the scale of the destruction in Tibet, the most tightly controlled part of China even under normal circumstances. Only brief, state-controlled media reports about the floods have been allowed to circulate in China and the authorities have confirmed only three deaths there. Chinese reports have focused on rescue efforts.

In Nepal earlier on Friday, army helicopter rescue teams were working to free about 100 people trapped in a tunnel at a flooded hydropower project.

Map showing location of the disaster

“Our focus is in search and rescue of people … some people are trapped in the tunnel of Trishuli 3A hydropower project,” the Nepal army spokesperson, Raja Ram Basnet, said.

“Two helicopters have been dispatched but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel. Relief efforts are also under way to provide the rescued people what they need.”

The prime minister’s office said the army was working in challenging conditions and had rescued 350 workers and local people who were trapped in the tunnel.

Rescue teams reported finding bodies hundreds of miles downstream from the disaster zone in the Chitwan district of Nepal, near the Tibetan border. Dozens of injured people were transported to Kathmandu for advanced medical care and more than 100 people were rescued by Nepali army personnel in helicopters.

CCTV said 499 Chinese nationals and 555 foreigners had been transported out of the disaster zone as of Friday.

नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा पर बुधदिन भेल घातक आकस्मिक बाढ़ि सं बचि गेल लोक के खोजय वाला बचावकर्मी के मलबा बांध के उफनला के बाद पाछू हटय पड़ल अछि, जाहि सं ताजा बाढ़ि के खतरा बढ़ि गेल अछि.

तिब्बत के सीमा पर स्थित नेपाल के रसुवा जिला के निवासी नदी में संभावित उफान स बचय लेल ⁠शुक्रदिन पहाड़ी ढाल पर दौड़ैत देखल गेल छल, ⁠गवाह सब के अनुसार । नेपालक अधिकारी कम सँ कम ९० मिनट धरि बचाव अभियान रोकने छल सेना अधिकारी जानकारी देलनि ।

बुधदिन तिब्बत केरऽ सीमावर्ती केंद्र ग्यरोंग प॑ कीचड़ आरू मलबा के देवाल स॑ टकराबै के बाद बनलऽ झील, जेकरा स॑ भयावह आकस्मिक बाढ़ आबी गेलै जेकरा स॑ घाटी म॑ गरजतें हुअ॑ गाँव सब के सफाया होय गेलै ।

चीन केरऽ सरकारी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी न॑ शुक्रवार क॑ खबर देलकै कि झील केरऽ फटै के खतरा के वजह स॑ चीनी बचावकर्मी आरू गाड़ी सुरक्षित क्षेत्र म॑ वापस आबी गेलऽ छेलै ।

नेपाल सीमा के पास पहाड़ के आधार पर बैरियर झील बनैत अछि |

बाढ़ि सं मृतक के पुष्टि भेल – जे ग्लेशियर के ढहला सं शुरू भेल छल – शुक्रदिन नेपाल में बढ़ि क 469 भ गेल, जाहि सं ओतय आ तिब्बत में 1300 सं बेसी लोक लापता अछि. चीन के अधिकारी सब एखन धरि पांच गोटे के मौत के पुष्टि क चुकल अछि।

नेपाल मे लापता ८२६ गोटे मे ५०० सँ बेसी विदेशी नागरिक रहल पुलिस आ पर्यटन ⁠अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, जाहि मे भारतक १७७, अमेरिकाक ९०, ऑस्ट्रेलियाक ३४, ब्रिटेन सँ ३३ आ कनाडा सँ २५ गोटे शामिल अछि । चीनी सरकारी मीडिया के कहनाय छनि जे सीमा के तिब्बत तरफ कम सं कम 558 लोक लापता छथिन्ह, जाहि मे सं कम सं कम 260 विदेशी नागरिक छथिन्ह.

जलवायु संकट के कारण नेपाल सन पहाड़ी क्षेत्र अस्थिर भ सकैत अछि, विशेषज्ञ सब चेतावनी देलनि Read more

बुधदिन बाढ़ि मे काठमांडू कए तिब्बत क ल्हासा स जोड़य वाला आ ट्रेकर्स आ तीर्थयात्री क बीच ⁠लोकप्रिय मार्ग क बिजली स्टेशन, सड़क आ पुल सब नष्ट भ गेल छल।

एकरऽ बाद मलबा स॑ बैरियर झील बनी गेलऽ छेलै जेकरा स॑ आरू बाढ़ के खतरा छेलै । चीन न॑ गुरुवार क॑ झील केरऽ हवाई सर्वेक्षण आरू थ्रीडी मॉडलिंग करै लेली आठ सदस्यीय इंजीनियरिंग टीम क॑ जुटान॑ छेलै आरू शुक्रवार तलक ओकरऽ जलाशय २.५ मीटर घन मीटर पानी के शीर्ष पर पहुँची गेलऽ छेलै, जे इंजीनियरिंग टीम न॑ एक दिन पहलें दर्ज करलऽ गेलऽ अनुमानित १.५-२ मीटर घन मीटर स॑ अधिक छै ।

नेपाल के बागमती प्रांत के नुकावोट जिला के राजधानी बिदुर में शुक्रदिन भोर में चीन सीमा के पास झील के किनारे फटला के बाद त्रिशुली नदी फेर सं बढ़य लागल छल.

बचावकर्मी क॑ इलाका स॑ हटाय देलऽ गेलै आरू जे निवासी न॑ अपनऽ घरऽ स॑ जे कुछ बचलऽ छै ओकरा म॑ वापस ऐला के कोशिश करलकै ओकरा तुरंत फेर स॑ घरऽ स॑ बाहर निकलै लेली कहलऽ गेलै ।

कहियो त्रिशूली क कात मे चहल-पहल वाला शहर बिदुर आब खंडहर भ गेल अछि। बुधदिन भोरे नदी घाटी मे थाल... चट्टान आ मलबा के ज्वार उमड़ला सं बेसि घर बह गेल. बचि गेल लोक सभ भवन आ गाछ सं चिपकल रहबाक वर्णन केलनि, जखन कि पानि ओकरा पर दौड़ैत छल.

एकटा बैंक, सरकारी कार्यालय आ एटीएम बूथ क टूटल-फूटल कंक्रीटक अवशेष ओहि किछु संरचना मे शामिल छल, हालांकि ओ थाल मे डूबल छल। अधिकारी के कहनाय छनि जे भवन के अंदर एखनो लाश अछि मुदा ओकरा बरामद करनाय बहुत खतरनाक अछि.

पास मे स्थानीय लोक थाल-कादो वाला सड़क पर जमा भ गेल छल, हेरायल रिश्तेदार के आवाज दैत छल आ अपन सामान के जे किछु बचल छल ओकरा खोदय के कोशिश करैत छल.

फ्लैश फ्लड स त्रस्त अधिकांश इलाका केवल सेना क हेलीकॉप्टर स पहुंचल रहल। बिदुर सेना शिविर म॑, जहां बचाव केरऽ बहुत सारा प्रयास के समन्वय होय रहलऽ छेलै, हर पांच मिनट प॑ बचाव आरू सैन्य हेलीकॉप्टर अंदर-बाहर उड़ै छेलै, जेकरा स॑ दर्जनों आहत पीड़ित आबै छेलै । बहुतो गोटे कहलनि जे किछुए मिनट मे बाढ़ि हुनकर प्रियजन, घर आ सब किछु ल' गेल छल.

अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय समुदाय नेपाल आ तिब्बतके बाढिसँ ग्रस्त भागमे सहायता प्राप्त करबाक लेल दौड़ल अछि ।

View image in fullscreen नुवाकोट जिला में फ्लैश फ्लड के बाद घरों में कीचड़ डूबी | फोटोग्राफ : एएफपी / गेटी इमेजेज

नेपाल न॑ कहलकै कि ओकरा अभी तलक विदेशी सहायता के जरूरत नै छै, कैन्हेंकि ई खोज-बचाव अभियान – जे पहाड़ी क्षेत्र भर म॑ दर्जनों पुल आरू मील-मील सड़क के नष्ट होय के कारण जटिल होय गेलऽ छै – जारी छै ।

विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता लोक बहादुर क्षेत्री शुक्रदिन कहलनि जे, मदद के प्रस्ताव स्वाभाविक अछि। ओ कहला जे हमर सुरक्षा एजेंसी सर्च एंड रेस्क्यू ऑपरेशन क रहल अछि। फिलहाल हमरा सभ केँ एहन मदद’क आवश्यकता नहि अछि.”

जेनेवा स्थित संयुक्त राष्ट्रमे नेपाली ⁠राजदूत रहल दिनेश भट्टराई कहलनि जे, सरकारक विदेशी सहायता स्वीकार करबा मे अनिच्छा रसुवा जिला आ चीनक तिब्बत क्षेत्रक संग ओकर सीमा पर संवेदनशीलता सँ जुड़ल भ’ सकैत अछि।

चीनी अधिकारियऽ स॑ सामान्य परिस्थिति म॑ भी चीन केरऽ सबस॑ कड़ा नियंत्रण वाला हिस्सा तिब्बत म॑ विनाश केरऽ पैमाना के बारे म॑ बहुत कम जानकारी सामने ऐलऽ छै । चीन म॑ बाढ़ के बारे म॑ खाली संक्षिप्त, राज्य नियंत्रित मीडिया रिपोर्ट क॑ ही घूमै के अनुमति देलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू अधिकारियऽ न॑ वहाँ महज तीन मौत के पुष्टि करलकै । चीनी रिपोर्ट बचाव प्रयास पर केंद्रित अछि।

title: What to know about the Mount Kailash pilgrimage site after floods in Nepal and Tibet - AP News
description: What to know about the Mount Kailash pilgrimage site after floods in Nepal and Tibet  AP News
publisher.title: AP News
full_article:
BEIJING (AP) — Devotees on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash — a sacred site in the Himalayas -- were among the many people missing after the massive floods along the border between Nepal and China.

Here’s what to know about the mountain and its centuries-old role as a pilgrimage site.

Mount Kailash is sacred for several religious traditions

Mount Kailash is a Himalayan peak in southwestern Tibet , near China’s borders with Nepal and India. It rises more than 6,400 meters (21,000 feet) above sea level and lies close to Lake Manasarovar. Both have long been part of Sanskrit religious and literary traditions.

Mount Kailash holds sacred significance for Hinduism , Buddhism , Jainism and the Tibetan Bon tradition. Each associates the mountain with different beliefs and sacred histories.

According to the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development, the mountain is considered the home of Shiva , the Hindu god of destruction, and Parvati, a Hindu goddess associated with marriage, fertility and motherhood.

Followers of the Tibetan Bon tradition regard it as a seat of spiritual power and associate the region with Tonpa Shenrab, the tradition’s founder.

Geographer Emily Yeh, a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder, who has conducted research in Tibet, wrote in 2017 that Kailash is associated with the mythical Mount Meru, considered the center of the world in Hindu and Buddhist cosmology.

The surrounding landscape also figures in local legends and Himalayan traditions. “Shared Sacred Landscapes,” a book published by ICIMOD in 2017, gathers some of them.

One story tells of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism , who visits villagers longing to make the pilgrimage to Mount Kailash. Nanak teaches them that the true pilgrimage is a spiritual journey within themselves.

Pilgrims travel to the mountain for purification

India’s government operates an official Kailash Manasarovar pilgrimage from June through August or September each year, with routes through the states of Uttarakhand and Sikkim. Private operators also organize pilgrimages through Nepal.

Pilgrims traditionally walk around Mount Kailash rather than climb it, completing a roughly 33-mile (53-kilometer) circuit around the mountain.

The journey around the peak is believed to cleanse pilgrims of their sins and can take about three days to complete. Hindus and Buddhists traditionally circle the mountain clockwise, while followers of Bon travel counterclockwise.

At nearby Lake Manasarovar, some Hindu pilgrims bathe in its waters as a ritual of spiritual purification.

Yeh wrote that Tibetan pilgrims stop at monasteries and other sacred sites along the route, touching prayer beads or their foreheads to features believed to bear sacred imprints. Other rituals are meant to test a pilgrim’s merit, sin or fortune.

Pilgrims are among the missing after floods

The death toll for the disaster continues to grow, and hundreds more are missing in Nepal and China.

The missing include at least 178 people from India, most of whom were believed to be on the pilgrimage. The missing also includes people from U.S., Australia, Britain and Canada.

Indian spiritual guru Jaggi Vasudev, also known as Sadhguru, said in a post on X that 77 people returning from the mountain with groups organized by his Isha Foundation were at an immigration center in Gyirong, Tibet, when the floods struck.

येह लिखलकै कि तिब्बती तीर्थयात्री मार्ग के साथ मठ आरू अन्य पवित्र स्थलऽ प॑ रुकी क॑ प्रार्थना के मोती या ओकरऽ कपार क॑ ऐन्हऽ विशेषता प॑ छूबै छै जेकरा प॑ पवित्र छाप मानलऽ जाय छै । अन्य संस्कारक उद्देश्य कोनो तीर्थयात्रीक पुण्य, पाप वा भाग्यक परीक्षा होइत छैक |

बाढ़ि के बाद लापता मे तीर्थयात्री सेहो शामिल छथिन्ह

आपदा के कारण मृतक के संख्या बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, आरू नेपाल आरू चीन म॑ सैकड़ों लोग आरू लापता छै ।

लापता मे भारत के कम सं कम 178 लोक शामिल छथिन्ह, जाहि मे सं बेसि लोक के तीर्थ यात्रा पर मानल गेल छल. लापता मे अमेरिका, ऑस्ट्रेलिया, ब्रिटेन आ कनाडा के लोक सेहो शामिल छथिन्ह.

भारतीय आध्यात्मिक गुरु जग्गी वासुदेव, जेकरा सद्गुरु के नाम स॑ भी जानलऽ जाय छै, न॑ एक्स प॑ एगो पोस्ट म॑ कहलकै कि हुनकऽ ईशा फाउंडेशन द्वारा आयोजित समूह के साथ पहाड़ स॑ वापस आबै वाला ७७ लोग तिब्बत केरऽ ग्यिरोंग म॑ एगो आप्रवासन केंद्र प॑ छेलै, जब॑ बाढ़ आबी गेलै ।

title: How Nepali diaspora is responding to flood disaster and how Australians can help in relief effort - The Guardian
description: How Nepali diaspora is responding to flood disaster and how Australians can help in relief effort  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
Australia’s Nepali community plan to host vigils to remember the victims of the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster to coincide with a day of mourning, as the number of people killed continues to rise.

As Australia’s Nepali diaspora wait for the full scale of the disaster to become clear, community members are desperately waiting to hear from missing relatives and friends.



Nepal police said on Friday that the death toll had risen to 469, with more than 1,300 people still missing, after massive flash floods and landslides tore through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river basins on Wednesday.

‘We just want them to return’: relatives of Australians missing in Nepal floods wait anxiously for news of loved ones Read more

The foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, on Friday morning confirmed the number of Australians missing in the floods had increased to 39 as she unveiled a $5m support package.

Wong told the ABC that Australians who wished to donate could do so via the Emergency Action Alliance website – run by a group of Australian charities and humanitarian organisations.

Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email

Nepali Australians gathered for candlelight prayers on Thursday night and held a minute’s silence for those lost to the floods.

Dr Tilak Pokhrel, president of the Australian Nepalese Multicultural Centre (ANMC), said community organisations in Victoria would host a vigil when the Nepali government announced an upcoming national day of mourning.

“Community members just want to say we are with you for those who are affected,” he said.

“We want to have an event where we all can gather and show our solidarity to support them.

“Let’s work together, let’s pray together, and let’s go through this pain together.”

View image in fullscreen Candles arranged in the shape of the Nepali flag at prayers in Rockdale, Sydney. Photograph: George Chan/AAP

Pokhrel said the centre would extend its opening hours for the next few days so faith leaders could provide support.

“People are waiting for the news. They are checking the news every hour,” he said.

Chudamani Sapkota, the general secretary of Non-Resident Nepali Association, said its New South Wales branch would host a candlelight vigil on Saturday evening in Sydney.

“This is devastating news for all the Nepalese diaspora,” he said.

Sapkota said the organisation was trying to support Nepali Australians seeking to locate their missing relatives.

“There’s no network, nothing at the moment,” he said. “This is a very tough time.”

Melbourne student Rakshya Pandey’s family home and two grocery shops in the Nuwakot district, hit by the flash flooding, have been destroyed. Her father, who was injured after being struck by an object in the flooding, is receiving treatment in a Kathmandu hospital.

“Whenever I see the detail of the people missing or the flood or everything, it’s just so scary, and I’m scared … I can’t do anything. I feel so helpless,” she said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Pandey fears there will be future flooding in Nepal.

Ashok Bahadur Dhungel, who lives in Canberra, has been trying to reach his nephew who works for the Upper Trishuli hydropower plant, which sat on one of the Nepali rivers that flooded. He said his nephew has not been online for two days.

“We hope he is still alive,” he said.

View image in fullscreen Melbourne student Rakshya Pandey (far right) with her family. The family’s home was destroyed by the floods that hit Nepal’s Nuwakot district. Photograph: supplied

Dhungel heard through friends that his mother, who lives in the Nuwakot district, had survived. But he has been unable to speak to her due to power outages.

“She is everything to me,” he said.

Tenzin Khangsar, co-chair of the Australia Tibet Council, said the Tibetan community was “shocked and devastated” about the flooding. He said prayer events would be planned to commemorate the victims.

Diaspora community organisations are also crowdfunding for the Nepali government’s disaster relief fund.

Climate crisis could be destabilising mountain areas like Nepal, experts warn Read more

Chiran Tiwari, president of the Nepalese Welfare Society based in Sydney, said the organisation had created a GoFundMe page to raise money for the Nepali prime minister’s natural disaster relief fund.

Tiwari said one of the welfare society’s executive member’s relatives was missing in Nepal, with the community rallying around to provide support to them.

“The situation is very sad for the community,” he said. “Everyone’s eyes is tearing so the situation is very difficult.”

On Thursday night, the ANMC hosted a candlelight multi-faith prayer night in Melbourne for people grieving the disaster.

ऑस्ट्रेलिया केरऽ नेपाली समुदाय न॑ शोक के दिन के साथ संयोग स॑ नेपाल-तिब्बत बाढ़ आपदा के शिकार लोगऽ क॑ याद करै लेली जागरण के आयोजन करै के योजना बनयने छै, कैन्हेंकि मृतकऽ के संख्या म॑ लगातार बढ़ोत्तरी होय रहलऽ छै ।

जेना-जेना ऑस्ट्रेलिया केरऽ नेपाली प्रवासी आपदा केरऽ पूरा पैमाना साफ होय के इंतजार करी रहलऽ छै, समुदाय के लोग लापता रिश्तेदार आरू दोस्तऽ स॑ सुनै के बेताब इंतजार करी रहलऽ छै ।



बुधदिन भोटेकोशी आ त्रिशुली नदी बेसिन मे भारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ आ भूस्खलन के बाद मृतक के संख्या ४६९ भ गेल अछि, जाहि मे १३०० सँ बेसी लोक अखनो लापता अछि, नेपाल प्रहरी शुक्रदिन जनौलक अछि ।

‘हमरा सब बस चाहैत छी जे ओ सब वापस आबि जाय’: नेपाल बाढ़ि मे लापता ऑस्ट्रेलियाई के रिश्तेदार अपन प्रियजन के खबर के बेचैनी स इंतजार क रहल छथि Read more

विदेश मंत्री पेनी वोंग न॑ शुक्रवार क॑ सुबह ई बात के पुष्टि करलकै कि बाढ़ म॑ लापता ऑस्ट्रेलियाई के संख्या बढ़ी क॑ ३९ होय गेलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि हुनी ५ मिलियन डॉलर के सहायता पैकेज के अनावरण करलकै ।

वोंग न॑ एबीसी क॑ बतैलकै कि जे ऑस्ट्रेलियाई दान करना चाहै छै, वू इमरजेंसी एक्शन एलायंस वेबसाइट के माध्यम स॑ ई काम करी सकै छै – जे ऑस्ट्रेलियाई चैरिटी आरू मानवीय संगठनऽ के एगो समूह द्वारा चलाबै छै ।

ब्रेकिंग न्यूज ऑस्ट्रेलिया ईमेल के लेल साइन अप करू

बृहस्पति दिन राति मे नेपाली ऑस्ट्रेलियाई लोकनि मोमबत्तीक रोशनी मे प्रार्थना लेल जमा भेलाह आ बाढ़ि मे हारल लोकक लेल एक मिनटक मौन रखलनि ।

ऑस्ट्रेलियाई नेपाली बहुसांस्कृतिक केन्द्र (एएनएमसी) के अध्यक्ष डॉ. तिलक पोखरेल कहलनि जे, जखन नेपाली सरकार आगामी राष्ट्रीय शोक दिवस के घोषणा करत तखन विक्टोरिया के सामुदायिक संस्था सब जागरण के आयोजन करत।

ओ कहला जे समुदाय क लोक बस इ कहय चाहैत छथि जे प्रभावित लोक लेल हम अहां सबहक संग छी।

ओ कहला जे हम चाहैत छी जे एहन आयोजन होए जाहि मे हम सब जमा भ सकब आ हुनकर समर्थन करबा लेल अपन एकजुटता देखा सकब।

“चलू, मिलिकय काज करी, एक संग प्रार्थना करी, आ एहि पीड़ा सँ मिलिकय गुजरी।”

फुलस्क्रीन में छवि देखें सिडनी के रॉकडेल में प्रार्थना में नेपाली झंडा के आकार में व्यवस्थित मोमबत्ती | फोटोग्राफ : जॉर्ज चान / आप

पोखरेल कहलनि जे, केंद्र अगिला किछु दिन तक अपन खुलबाक समय बढ़ा देत जाहि सं आस्था के नेता सहयोग क सकय।

ओ कहला जे लोक एहि खबर क इंतजार मे अछि। हर घंटा समाचार चेक क रहल छथि।'

गैर निवासी नेपाली संघक महासचिव चूडामणि सापकोटा कहलनि जे, हुनकर न्यू साउथ वेल्स शाखा शनिदिन साँझ सिडनी मे मोमबत्ती जरा कए जागरण करत।

ओ कहलनि जे, ई समस्त नेपाली प्रवासी लेल विनाशकारी खबर अछि।

सापकोटा कहलनि जे, संस्था अपन लापता रिश्तेदार के खोजय चाहय वाला नेपाली ऑस्ट्रेलियाई के सहयोग करय के कोशिश क रहल अछि।

ओ कहलनि, “कोनो नेटवर्क नहि अछि, एखन किछु नहि अछि.” “ई बहुत कठिन समय अछि।”

मेलबर्न केरऽ छात्रा रक्षा पांडेय केरऽ पारिवारिक घर आरू नुवाकोट जिला म॑ दू किराना दुकान, जेकरा प॑ फ्लैश फ्लडिंग न॑ चपेट म॑ आबी गेलऽ छै, तबाह होय गेलऽ छै । बाढ़िमे कोनो वस्तुसँ टकराएल हुनकर पिताके काठमाण्डौ अस्पतालमे उपचार भऽ रहल अछि ।

“जखन कखनो लोकक लापता वा बाढ़ि वा सब किछुक डिटेल देखैत छी त’ बस एतेक डरावना होइत अछि, आ हम डरा जाइत छी ... हम किछु नहि क’ सकैत छी. हम अपना के एतेक लाचार महसूस करैत छी।'

पाण्डेय के आशंका अछि जे भविष्य मे नेपाल मे बाढ़ि आओत.

कैनबरा मे रहनिहार अशोक बहादुर ढुंगेल अपन भतीजा जे अपर त्रिशुली जलविद्युत संयंत्र मे काज करैत छथि, जे नेपाली नदी मे स एकटा नदी पर बैसल छल, तक पहुंचबाक प्रयास मे लागल छथि। ओ कहलनि जे, हुनकर भतीजा दू दिन सं ऑनलाइन नहि छथि।

ओ कहला जे हमरा सब कए उम्मीद अछि जे ओ एखनो जीवित छथि।

फुलस्क्रीन में छवि देखू मेलबर्न के छात्रा रक्षा पांडेय (सबसे दाहिना) अपन परिवार के संग। नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला मे आयल बाढ़ि मे परिवार के घर तबाह भ गेल. फोटोग्राफ: आपूर्ति कयल गेल

ढुंगेल दोस्त सब के माध्यम स सुनलक जे ओकर माय जे नुवाकोट जिला में रहैत अछि, बचल अछि। मुदा बिजली कटौती के कारण ओ हुनका सं बात नहि क सकल छथिन्ह.

ओ कहलनि जे, ओ हमरा लेल सब किछु छथि।

ऑस्ट्रेलिया तिब्बत परिषद केरऽ सह-अध्यक्ष तेनज़िन खंगसर न॑ कहलकै कि तिब्बती समुदाय बाढ़ स॑ “हतब आरू तबाह” छै । ओ कहलनि जे, पीड़ित के याद मे प्रार्थना के आयोजन के योजना बनाओल जायत।

प्रवासी सामुदायिक संगठन सेहो नेपाली सरकार के आपदा राहत कोष के लेल क्राउडफंडिंग क रहल अछि.

जलवायु संकट के कारण नेपाल सन पहाड़ी क्षेत्र अस्थिर भ सकैत अछि, विशेषज्ञ सब चेतावनी देलनि Read more

सिडनी स्थित नेपाली वेलफेयर सोसाइटी के अध्यक्ष चिरन तिवारी कहलनि जे, संस्था नेपाली प्रधानमंत्री के प्राकृतिक आपदा राहत कोष के लेल पैसा जुटेबाक लेल GoFundMe पेज बनौलक अछि।

तिवारी कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे कल्याणकारी संस्थाक कार्यकारिणी सदस्यक एकटा परिजन लापता अछि, जाहि मे समुदाय हुनका सभक सहयोग देबाक लेल इम्हर-उम्हर जुटि गेल अछि।

ओ कहलनि जे, समाज के लेल स्थिति बहुत दुखद अछि। “सबक आँखि नोचि रहल अछि तेँ स्थिति बहुत कठिन अछि।”

गुरुवार के रात एएनएमसी न॑ मेलबर्न म॑ आपदा स॑ दुखी लोगऽ लेली मोमबत्ती के रोशनी म॑ बहु-आस्था प्रार्थना रात के आयोजन करलकै ।

title: ‘Immense impact’ of Nepal flood disaster highlighted as casualties mount - UN News
description: ‘Immense impact’ of Nepal flood disaster highlighted as casualties mount  UN News
publisher.title: UN News
full_article:
The catastrophic flooding occurred at the border between Nepal and the Tibet autonomous region of China.

It is thought to have been caused by the collapse of a glacier and the resulting landslide, leading to the destruction of entire communities as well as key infrastructure including bridges and roads.

On Friday, quoting Government of Nepal figures the UN’s aid coordination office OCHA said that 538 people had died, while almost 3,750 had been rescued. Around 1000 people are still missing, many of whom are thought to be tourists.

The Tibet autonomous region of China was also affected and some 560 people remain missing there, according to the authorities.

Tweet URL

Lila Pieters Yahia, the UN Resident Coordinator in Nepal who visited the disaster zone said the search and rescue effort was ongoing.

“We witnessed people had just been rescued as we were walking and visiting the site, one of the sites which has been severely damaged,” she said. “We saw a whole truck full of people, an entire family had just been rescued and I can tell you it was very, very emotional.”

Her visit was cut short after a renewed flood alert was issued.

Relief effort

Aid teams have been working around the clock to reach communities cut off by the disaster in the Nepalese districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading.

© UNICEF/Robic Upadhayay Emergency supplies are prepared for delivery to flood-affected communities in Nepal.

The UN is supporting the relief effort with emergency food rations, medical kits for about 10,000 people for three months, as well as tents and logistics support. It is also providing satellite imagery and analysis of the area affected by the flood.

Meanwhile, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned of the risk of disease. “As always, when we have disaster of this scale and we have displacement, overcrowding, and we may have disruption of water, sanitation and health services, and that can increase the risk of infectious diseases,” said spokesperson Tarik Jašarević in Geneva.

UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) spokesperson Ricardo Pires told reporters that while 18 schools have been completely destroyed and another 20 have been damaged, “dozens more are located close to the riverbanks and remain at high risk,” meaning an estimated 10,000 school-aged children in the area need support to continue their education.

Disaster-affected region

The area was hit by a 7.8 magnitude earthquake in April 2015, which killed more than 8,800 people.

Last October, torrential rains caused fast-moving floods and landslides across eastern and central Nepal, affecting more than 30,000 people.

Kamal Kishore, the Head of the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) highlighted the seriousness of the disaster. “In living memory, we haven't seen a mountain hazard event like this for a very, very long time,” he said, adding that “the impact on lives, livelihoods, buildings, infrastructure, bridges, hydroelectric projects, power generation, it's really immense. And I think we are still coming to grips with the extent of the damage.”

He added that the current situation is marked by “extremely high risk as well as a lot of uncertainty.”

“It's a unique challenge for the emergency response itself, because in a sense, the disaster is not yet completely over,” he stressed.

The floods have “again highlighted how fragile mountain ecosystems are and how challenging it is to set up early warning systems in mountain environments,” focusing on a range of cascading hazards.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) which is working alongside the UN in Nepal said it was “very, very concerned about the secondary flood.”

The IFRC believes that at least 93,000 people have been affected and are “in great need.”

नेपाल आ चीन के तिब्बत स्वायत्त क्षेत्र के सीमा पर विनाशकारी बाढ़ि आयल अछि।

मानलऽ जाय छै कि एकरऽ कारण ग्लेशियर केरऽ ढहला आरू एकरऽ परिणामस्वरूप भूस्खलन होय ​​गेलऽ छै, जेकरा चलतें पूरा समुदाय के साथ-साथ पुल आरू सड़क सहित प्रमुख बुनियादी ढाँचा के भी नष्ट होय गेलऽ छै ।

शुक्रदिन नेपाल सरकार के आंकड़ा के हवाला दैत संयुक्त राष्ट्र के सहायता समन्वय कार्यालय ओसीएचए कहलनि जे, 538 लोक के मौत भ गेल अछि, जखन कि लगभग 3,750 के बचाओल गेल अछि। करीब 1000 लोक एखनो लापता छथि, जाहि मे सं बहुतो के पर्यटक मानल जाइत अछि.

चीन केरऽ तिब्बत स्वायत्त क्षेत्र भी प्रभावित होय गेलै आरू वहाँ लगभग ५६० लोग लापता छै, अधिकारियऽ के अनुसार ।

ट्वीट यूआरएल

आपदा क्षेत्रमे गेल नेपालमे संयुक्त राष्ट्रसंघके निवासी समन्वयक लीला पीटर्स याहिया खोज आ बचाव प्रयास जारी रहल बतौलनि ।

ओ कहली जे हम सब देखलहुं जे एखनहि लोक कए बचाउल गेल छल, जखन हम सब पैदल चलैत छलहुं आ एहि स्थल पर जा रहल छलहुं, जे ओहि स्थल मे स एक अछि जे काफी क्षतिग्रस्त भ गेल अछि। “हमरा लोकनि एकटा पूरा ट्रक लोक सँ भरल देखलहुँ, एकटा पूरा परिवार केँ एखनहि बचाओल गेल छल आ हम अहाँ केँ कहि सकैत छी जे ई बहुत, बहुत भावुक छल।”

नयका बाढ़ अलर्ट जारी भेलाक बाद हुनकर यात्रा कम भ गेल।

राहत प्रयास

नेपालक रसुवा, नुवाकोट आ धादिङ जिल्लामे आपदासँ कटल समुदाय तक पहुँचबामे सहायता दल चौबीसों घंटा कार्यरत रहल अछि ।

© यूनिसेफ/रोबिक उपाध्याय नेपाल मे बाढ़ि प्रभावित समुदाय मे आपातकालीन सामान पहुँचेबाक लेल तैयार कएल गेल अछि ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र आपातकालीन भोजन राशन, तीन महीना तक लगभग 10,000 लोगऽ लेली मेडिकल किट के साथ-साथ टेंट आरू रसद सहायता के साथ राहत प्रयास के समर्थन करी रहलऽ छै । संगहि बाढ़ि सं प्रभावित इलाका के उपग्रह इमेजरी आओर विश्लेषण सेहो द रहल अछि.

एम्हर विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन (डब्ल्यूएचओ) बीमारी के खतरा के चेतावनी देलक अछि। जेनेवा मँ प्रवक्ता तारिक जाशारेविच नँ कहलकै, “हमेशा के तरह, जबे हमरा सब के पास ई पैमाना के आपदा आबै छै आरू हमरा सब के पास विस्थापन, भीड़भाड़ छै, आरू हमरा पास पानी, स्वच्छता आरू स्वास्थ्य सेवा मँ बाधा आबी सकै छै, आरू जेकरा स॑ संक्रामक बीमारी के खतरा बढ़ी सकै छै ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र बाल कोष (यूनिसेफ) केरऽ प्रवक्ता रिकार्डो पाइरेस न॑ पत्रकारऽ स॑ कहलकै कि जहां १८ स्कूल पूरा तरह स॑ नष्ट होय गेलऽ छै आरू २० आरू क्षतिग्रस्त होय गेलऽ छै, वहीं “दर्जनों आरू स्कूल नदी के किनारे के नजदीक स्थित छै आरू उच्च जोखिम म॑ छै,” मतलब कि ई क्षेत्र केरऽ लगभग १०,००० स्कूली उम्र के बच्चा सिनी क॑ अपनऽ शिक्षा जारी रखै लेली सहायता के जरूरत छै ।

आपदा प्रभावित क्षेत्र

ई क्षेत्र म॑ अप्रैल २०१५ म॑ ७.८ तीव्रता के भूकंप आबी गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा म॑ ८,८०० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

पिछला अक्टूबर मे मूसलाधार वर्षा के कारण पूर्वी आ मध्य नेपाल मे तेजी सं बाढ़ि आ भूस्खलन भेल छल जाहि सं 30 हजार सं बेसि लोक प्रभावित भेल छल.

संयुक्त राष्ट्र आपदा जोखिम कम करय के कार्यालय (यूएनडीआरआर) के प्रमुख कमल किशोर आपदा के गंभीरता पर प्रकाश डाललखिन्ह. ओ कहलनि जे, जीवित स्मृति मे हम सब बहुत, बहुत लंबा समय स एहि तरहक पहाड़ी खतरा क घटना नहि देखलहुं अछि, आ इहो कहलनि जे, “जीवन, आजीविका, भवन, बुनियादी ढांचा, पुल, जलविद्युत परियोजना, बिजली उत्पादन पर एकर असर सचमुच अपार अछि।आ हमरा लगैत अछि जे हम सब एखनो नुकसान क हद पर काबू पाबि रहल छी।”

हुनी आरू कहलकै कि वर्तमान स्थिति म॑ “अत्यंत उच्च जोखिम के साथ-साथ बहुत अनिश्चितता भी छै ।”

हुनी जोर देलकै कि आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया लेली ही ई एगो अनूठा चुनौती छै, कैन्हेंकि एक तरह स॑ ई आपदा अभी पूरा तरह स॑ खत्म नै होय सकलऽ छै ।

बाढ़ न॑ “फिर स॑ ई बात प॑ प्रकाश डाललकै कि पहाड़ी पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र कतेक नाजुक छै आरू पहाड़ी वातावरण म॑ जल्दी चेतावनी प्रणाली स्थापित करना कतेक चुनौतीपूर्ण छै,” जेकरा म॑ झरना के खतरा के एक श्रृंखला प॑ ध्यान देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

नेपालमे संयुक्त राष्ट्र संघक संग काज कऽ रहल अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय रेडक्रस आ रेड क्रिसेंट सोसाइटी महासंघ (आईएफआरसी) कहलक अछि जे ओ “गौण बाढ़िसँ बहुत, बहुत चिंतित अछि ।”

आईएफआरसी के मानना ​​छै कि कम स॑ कम ९३,००० लोगऽ क॑ प्रभावित करलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू ओकरा “बहुत जरूरत छै” ।

title: Tennessee-based nonprofit group caught in Nepal flooding, 22 Americans among travelers - WTVC
description: Tennessee-based nonprofit group caught in Nepal flooding, 22 Americans among travelers  WTVC
publisher.title: WTVC
full_article:
McMINNVILLE, Tenn. — A Tennessee-connected nonprofit is working to account for dozens of Americans after a pilgrimage group was caught in catastrophic flooding near the Nepal-Tibet border.

Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev, founder of the Isha Foundation, says about 80 people traveling with the group were caught in flash flooding near Mount Kailash, a destination considered sacred by several religions.

“We’ve sent messages to all the families,” Sadhguru said in a social media post.

Sadhguru says 22 of the travelers were from the United States.

People walk past damage in the aftermath of flash floods in Devighat in the Nuwakot district in Nepal, Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. (AP Photo/Niranjan Shrestha)

Leslie Crespi, a community liaison for Isha Foundation’s McMinnville center, says those Americans were affiliated with the Tennessee-based non-profit.

“They're like family to us,” Crespi says. “These are people that we knew and we volunteered alongside of for many years.”

The group’s ordeal comes as widespread flooding across Nepal and neighboring China has left hundreds dead and more than 1,000 people missing.

Reports indicate at least 90 Americans are among those missing across the region as search and rescue efforts continue.

This satellite image provided by Vantor shows destruction at Syapru Besi, Nepal on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. (Satellite image ©2026 Vantor via AP)

The flooding and devastation are believed to be connected to a glacier.

UTC Assistant Professor of Geology Jennifer Taylor says glaciers can hold massive amounts of water...

“When you look at these glaciers, think of them as filling entire valleys,” Taylor says. “They are holding a lot of water in the first place.”

Jenisha, right, cries as she waits for news on her father missing after flash flooding in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Friday, Aug. 28, 2026. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh)

Taylor says the region’s steep mountains can intensify flooding. The terrain can funnel water through narrow valleys, creating powerful and fast-moving walls of water

"That's where you're getting these very high, tall walls of water is because that water is not having a chance to spread out, but staying funneled in those really steep valleys."

This satellite image provided by Vantor shows the remains of a cement site in Nepal on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. (Satellite image 2026 Vantor via AP)

In a statement sent Friday evening, Isha Foundation says...

"Isha Foundation is deeply saddened by the devastating flash floods that have struck Gyirong in Tibet, near the Nepal-China border.

One of our Kailash Yatra groups was at the immigration center in Gyirong while returning from Kailash when the flash flood occurred. The immigration center and surrounding areas were severely impacted. At this time, we are awaiting official information regarding the whereabouts and wellbeing of those who were at the location...

Sadhguru, founder of Isha Foundation, along with volunteers across the globe and support teams in the region, is working closely with the concerned authorities and doing everything possible to support the ongoing search and rescue efforts. We request everyone to keep those affected in their thoughts and prayers and to rely only on verified updates from official sources. Our immediate priority is the safety and wellbeing of everyone affected. We are working urgently with relevant authorities and diplomatic representatives to confirm the status and whereabouts of those unaccounted for."

We have reached out to the Isha Foundation's base in McMinnville to discover if any of those Americans involved lived in Tennessee. So far we have not heard back yet.

Depend on us to keep you posted.

WTVC

जेनिशा, दाहिना, नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला में फ्लैश फ्लड के बाद अपन पिता के लापता होय के खबर के इंतजार में कानि रहल छथि, शुक्र दिन, 28 अगस्त 2026. (एपी फोटो/राजेश कुमार सिंह)

हमर कैलाश यात्रा समूह मे स एकटा कैलाश स घुरैत काल ग्यरोंग क इमिग्रेशन सेंटर मे छल जखन झटका बाढ़ि आयल। आप्रवासन केंद्र आ आसपास के इलाका पर बहुत असर पड़ल। एहि समय हम सब ओहि स्थान पर रहनिहार लोकनिक ठिकाना आ भलाई के संबंध मे आधिकारिक जानकारी के इंतजार क रहल छी...

हम मैकमिंविले में ईशा फाउंडेशन के बेस तक पहुंचि गेलहुं अछि जे एहि सं जुड़ल ओहि अमेरिकी में सं कियो टेनेसी में रहैत छल कि नहिं. एखन धरि हम सब एखन धरि कोनो जवाब नहि सुनने छी।

अहाँ सब के पोस्ट करैत रहबाक लेल हमरा सब पर निर्भर रहू।

title: Pope Leo prays for victims of devastating Nepal floods - Vatican News
description: Pope Leo prays for victims of devastating Nepal floods  Vatican News
publisher.title: Vatican News
full_article:
Vatican News

Pope Leo XIV has expressed his deep sorrow over the loss of life and widespread devastation caused by flash floods in Nepal.

In a telegram sent on Thursday and signed by Cardinal Secretary of State Pietro Parolin, the Pope commended the souls of those who died “to the clemency of the Almighty” and offered his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved.

He also assured all those affected by the disaster of his spiritual closeness and prayed for the emergency personnel engaged in the ongoing search-and-rescue operations.

The telegram concluded with the Pope's prayers for God’s assistance and protection upon the people of Nepal.

Hundreds dead or missing

Over 350 people have died in Nepal, while more than 900 remain unaccounted for after a devastating torrent of water, mud and debris swept through communities near the country’s northern border with China. Unfortunately, the death toll is expected to rise as bodies are recovered from under the debris.

Hundreds more are missing in neighbouring Tibet, bringing the total number of people unaccounted for across the affected region to almost 1,500.

The disaster is believed to have been triggered by the collapse of part of a Himalayan glacier, which sent a sudden surge into a river system along the Nepal-China border. Scientists said the force of the collapse was so great that the resulting tremors were initially mistaken for an earthquake.

Entire settlements were inundated, while roads, bridges, power installations and other essential infrastructure were destroyed or severely damaged. The floods also struck a major border crossing, cutting off transport and trade routes.

Many of those missing are foreign visitors who had travelled to the region on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar, sites considered sacred by Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and followers of the Bon religion.

Rescue operations continue

Thousands of soldiers, police officers and emergency workers have been deployed across the affected areas. Helicopters are being used to reach isolated communities, evacuate survivors and deliver food, medical supplies and other forms of emergency assistance.

Operations are being complicated by damaged roads, difficult mountainous terrain and the continuing danger of landslides and further flooding.

International aid has begun to arrive, with neighbouring countries, the United Nations and humanitarian organisations offering personnel, supplies and financial assistance.

The tragedy has also renewed concerns about the growing threat posed by glacial instability in the Himalayas, where rising temperatures are accelerating the melting and retreat of glaciers.
translated:
वैटिकन समाचार

पोप लियो चौदहवाँ नेपालमे झटका बाढ़ि सँ भेल जान-हानि आ व्यापक तबाही पर गहींर दुख व्यक्त केने छथि ।

गुरुवार क॑ भेजलऽ गेलऽ आरू कार्डिनल विदेश सचिव पिएत्रो पैरोलिन केरऽ हस्ताक्षर वाला तार म॑ पोप न॑ “सर्वशक्तिमान केरऽ दया” म॑ मरै वाला लोगऽ के आत्मा के प्रशंसा करलकै आरू शोक संतप्त लोगऽ के प्रति दिल स॑ संवेदना व्यक्त करलकै ।

आपदा स॑ प्रभावित सब लोगऽ क॑ अपनऽ आध्यात्मिक निकटता के आश्वासन भी देलकै आरू जारी खोज-बचाव अभियान म॑ जुटलऽ आपातकालीन कर्मी सिनी लेली प्रार्थना करलकै ।

तार केरऽ समापन पोप केरऽ नेपाल केरऽ जनता प॑ भगवान केरऽ सहायता आरू सुरक्षा केरऽ प्रार्थना स॑ करलऽ गेलै ।

सैकड़ों मृत या लापता

चीन के साथ देश के उत्तरी सीमा के पास समुदायऽ म॑ पानी, थाल आरू मलबा के विनाशकारी धार बहला के बाद नेपाल म॑ ३५० स॑ अधिक लोगऽ के मौत होय चुकलऽ छै, जबकि ९०० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के हिसाब नै छै । दुर्भाग्यवश मलबा के नीचा सं लाश बरामद भेला सं मृतक के संख्या बढ़य के उम्मीद अछि.

पड़ोसी देश तिब्बत म॑ सैकड़ों आरू लोगऽ के लापता छै, जेकरा स॑ पूरा प्रभावित क्षेत्र म॑ बेहिसाब लोगऽ के संख्या लगभग १५०० होय गेलऽ छै ।

मानल जा रहल अछि जे ई आपदा हिमालयी ग्लेशियर के किछु हिस्सा के ढहला सं भेल अछि, जाहि सं नेपाल-चीन सीमा पर नदी प्रणाली मे अचानक उफान आबि गेल. वैज्ञानिक सब के कहनाय छनि जे एहि गिरय के बल एतेक बेसी छल जे एकर परिणामस्वरूप बनल भूकंप के शुरू मे भूकंप के गलती सं मानल गेल छल.

पूरा बस्ती बाढ़ि मे आबि गेल, जखन कि सड़क, पुल, बिजली स्थापना आ अन्य आवश्यक बुनियादी ढांचा नष्ट भ गेल या गंभीर रूप स क्षतिग्रस्त भ गेल। बाढ़ि के कारण एकटा पैघ सीमा क्रासिंग सेहो आबि गेल अछि, जाहि सं परिवहन आ व्यापारिक मार्ग बंद भ गेल.

लापता लोगऽ म॑ स॑ बहुत सारा विदेशी आगंतुक छै जे हिन्दू, बौद्ध, जैन आरू बोन धर्म के अनुयायी सिनी द्वारा पवित्र मानलऽ जाय वाला स्थल कैलाश पर्वत आरू मानसरोवर झील के तीर्थयात्रा प॑ ई क्षेत्र गेलऽ छेलै ।

बचाव कार्य जारी अछि

प्रभावित इलाका मे हजारों जवान, पुलिस अधिकारी आ आपातकालीन कार्यकर्ता के तैनाती कायल गेल अछि। हेलीकॉप्टर के उपयोग अलग-थलग समुदाय तक पहुंचै, बची गेलऽ लोगऽ क॑ बाहर निकालै आरू भोजन, चिकित्सा आपूर्ति आरू अन्य तरह के आपातकालीन सहायता पहुँचै लेली करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

सड़क क्षतिग्रस्त, कठिन पहाड़ी इलाका आ भूस्खलन आ आओर बाढ़ि के लगातार खतरा के कारण परिचालन जटिल भ रहल अछि.

अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सहायता केरऽ आगमन शुरू होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ पड़ोसी देश, संयुक्त राष्ट्र आरू मानवीय संगठन कर्मी, आपूर्ति आरू आर्थिक सहायता के पेशकश करी रहलऽ छै ।

ई त्रासदी न॑ हिमालय म॑ हिमनदी अस्थिरता के वजह स॑ बढ़तऽ खतरा के बारे म॑ भी चिंता क॑ नवीनीकरण करी देल॑ छै, जहां बढ़तऽ तापमान स॑ ग्लेशियरऽ के पिघलना आरू पीछे हटै म॑ तेजी आबी रहलऽ छै ।

full_article:
By Vatican News

After expressing, in a telegram, his deep sorrow over the devastating flooding in Nepal on Wednesday, August 26, Pope Leo XIV has sent concrete financial support, in coordination with the Apostolic Nunciature of Nepal, to meet the most urgent needs of the population affected by the disaster.

Read also 27/08/2026 Pope Leo prays for victims of devastating Nepal floods Pope Leo XIV expresses his sorrow over the loss of life caused by catastrophic flash floods in Nepal, assuring those affected of his spiritual closeness and praying for rescuers ...







The contribution will help Caritas Nepal, which operates under the direction of the Apostolic Vicariate, with the activities already underway since the first hours after the flood, namely providing immediate assistance with food, basic necessities, and shelter for those who have lost everything.

"This is the initial assistance that the Holy Father, as on other occasions, wanted to send to meet the immediate needs of the population,” explained the Prefect of the Dicastery for the Service of Charity, Archbishop Luis Marín de San Martín.

The Prefect called it "a rapid and concrete sign to convey, especially to the most vulnerable, the closeness and tenderness of the Holy Father, like a caress from the Church that accompanies and supports them."

The latest figures put the toll at more than 630 deaths and nearly 3,000 people, including over 500 foreigners, missing in the various affected regions. The Nepalese army has been deployed to help rescue more than 100 people believed to be trapped inside a hydroelectric power plant tunnel in the country’s hardest-hit district.

title: Rescuers search for thousands following deadly Nepal-China flood - CBC
description: Rescuers search for thousands following deadly Nepal-China flood  CBC
publisher.title: CBC
full_article:
As rescue efforts in communities buried by catastrophic flash floods along the border between Nepal and China entered their fourth day on Saturday, authorities continued finding survivors and transporting them to safety.

At relief centres, as some arrive, families wait anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of people unaccounted for continued to rise.

Chinese authorities have reported seven deaths and more than 550 missing, while Nepal's disaster agency said the death toll had climbed to 669 with 2,426 people missing.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far.

WATCH | Nepal-Tibet flash flood death toll continues to climb: Nepal-Tibet flash flood death toll climbs as fears of 2nd flood grow August 28 | Duration 2:21 CBC News is on the ground in Nepal, where fears are growing that a swollen artificial lake formed by this week's massive flash flood along the Tibet border could cause another flooding disaster. So far at least 579 people have been confirmed dead, while almost 2,000 are still missing.

In Nuwakot, one of the Nepali districts devastated by the floods, helicopters resumed operations before noon on Saturday after poor weather temporarily hampered aerial rescue activities.

Some helicopters were loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice. Others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors.

Villagers return to devastated homes

As people were still leaving Trishuli, some village residents were returning to see what could be salvaged from their decimated homes.

One boy walked out of the village carrying muddy sandals from his house. A woman, Shoba Shrestha, returned to find her dog, Sweetie, whom she was forced to leave behind when the floods came. Shrestha sat on the ground petting her and feeding her water from a bottle.

At some point, relief co-ordinators cleared villagers, reporters and volunteers from the entrance to Trishuli, as excavation equipment drove into the flooded village to dig.

Shoba Shrestha gives water to her dog, Sweetie, after the dog returned home on Saturday following four days apart in the aftermath of flash floods in Nepal's Nuwakot district. (Dar Yasin/The Associated Press)

Families begin to lose hope

In Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, relatives and friends gathered outside the main government hospital from early morning, desperately searching for news of missing loved ones.

Many shuffled between the help desk and the hospital notice board, clutching photographs and scanning injured patients' lists in the hope of finding them.

Dil Maya Lama stood weeping outside the help desk at the hospital, searching for information about her missing 26-year-old brother, a driver for a hydropower company in Rasuwa. She had travelled from Ramechhap, about 130 kilometres.

"I came here with the hope that I might find him," she said. "There is no information about him."

WATCH | Families of Canadians missing following flood still have hope: Families of Canadians missing in Nepal-Tibet flood cling to hope August 28 | Duration 1:55 Families of Canadians missing after the Nepal-Tibet flash flood disaster are desperate for any news of their loved ones, with some planning to travel to join the search efforts. Of the 32 Canadians reported missing, none have yet been confirmed dead.

Families covered hospital walls with posters showing missing relatives, photographs and contact numbers in a desperate appeal for any clue that could bring them home.

Nearby were photographs of unidentified bodies that officials put up in hopes they could be recognized by families or friends.

Gajendra Rawat, a security official at the hospital help desk, said families had so far registered about 1,600 missing persons since the disaster struck. "People are coming from all parts of Nepal," he said.

Video Families search for loved ones among the dead in Nepal

Video ‘Our community, our relatives, our friends’: GTA’s Nepalese community reacts to deadly floods

Back in Nuwakot, military personnel taped sheets of paper listing dozens of missing people to a wall at a relief centre, prompting families to crowd around them. Some scanned lists of the missing and dead, took photos and wiped away tears as they looked through the names.

Rajesh Kumar Ram desperately searched a list for his son's name.

"I'm hopeful, by chance, that my son is somewhere," he said, crying as he spoke. "Maybe they find him stuck somewhere. I'm waiting for that moment only."

Rescuers battle to find survivors in disaster-hit areas

Search-and-rescue efforts continued at several locations in Nepal and Tibet, including the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Nepal's Rasuwa district and the severely damaged Gyirong border crossing on the Chinese side.

Nepali army spokesperson Brig.-Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said rescue efforts would continue at the hydropower construction site, where authorities believe more than 100 people are trapped in a tunnel filled with thick mud.

Basnet said rescuers had used baskets and ropes to reach some people, but the operation remained difficult.

People crowd around to look at photographs of those killed in flash floods displayed outside a hospital to help relatives identify the victims, in Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, on Friday. (Dar Yasin/The Associated Press)

He said rescue teams had also been forced to relocate temporarily when authorities issued warnings about possible further flooding.

Rescuers have been on high alert for more flooding from a new lake that formed high up in the Himalayan mountains after the initial floods on Wednesday. Experts warned that the lake, created after a glacier collapse that triggered the floods, was starting to overflow.

Audio The disaster in Nepal as a ‘wake-up call from Mother Nature’

Monitoring data from the Chinese Ministry of Water Resources showed late Friday that the lake had dwindled in size. The water level dropped by 10 metres from a high point on Thursday morning, Chinese broadcaster CCTV said.

Aid trucks could be seen traveling from Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, toward the affected areas.

Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said on social media Saturday that a Canadian who was previously missing has been found safe.

Anand said there are still 31 Canadians still unaccounted for, noting the figure could still "fluctuate" as information becomes available.

Search continues at devastated China-Nepal border

The Chinese broadcaster showed images on Saturday of rescuers arriving at Gyirong Port, the hard-hit border crossing with Nepal. Some reached the area by foot or via rafts, while others dropped down from drones flown to the area. "Anyone, anyone?" rescuers yelled.

It was not immediately known how many people were at the border checkpoint building when the floods hit.

In this photo released by Xinhua News Agency, a drone carries cargo as search-and-rescue operations are underway at the mudslide-hit area in Gyirong County on Saturday. (Jiang Fan/Xinhua/The Associated Press)

On Saturday, Nepal's disaster agency said the death toll had climbed to 626, with 2,426 people missing in the country. More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far.

The death toll in China rose to seven on Friday as state media showed evacuations of villages and leaders' efforts to direct the relief response. China's state media said 554 people were missing on the Chinese side. Hundreds of the missing are foreigners who were in the area to work, trek or make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak.

बाढ़ि सँ तबाह नेपाली जिल्ला मे सँ एक नुवाकोट मे शनिदिन दुपहर सँ पहिने हेलीकॉप्टर के परिचालन शुरू भ गेल अछि, जखन कि खराब मौसम के कारण अस्थायी रूप सँ हवाई बचाव कार्य मे बाधा पहुँचल छल ।

किछु हेलीकॉप्टर मे कपड़ा, इंस्टेंट नूडल्स, पटाखा आ चावल सहित सहायताक बक्सा आ बैग लदल छल। दोसर लोक बाढ़ि प्रभावित इलाका स बचि गेल लोक कए ल कए वापस आबि गेल।

गामक लोक तबाह घर मे वापस आबि जाइत छथि

जखन कि लोक एखनो त्रिशूली स निकलि रहल छल, किछु गामक निवासी वापस आबि रहल छलाह जे हुनकर नष्ट घर स की बचाउल जा सकैत अछि।

एकटा छौड़ा अपन घरसँ थाल-कादोक चप्पल लऽ कऽ गामसँ बाहर निकलल। शोबा श्रेष्ठ नामक एकटा महिला अपन कुकुर स्वीटी के खोजय लेल वापस आबि गेलीह, जकरा बाढ़ि आबि गेला पर छोड़ि देबय लेल मजबूर भ गेल छलीह. श्रेष्ठ जमीन पर बैसल ओकरा पोसैत आ बोतल सँ पानि खुआबैत छल ।

कोनो समय राहत समन्वयक गामक लोक, रिपोर्टर आ स्वयंसेवक के त्रिशुली के प्रवेश द्वार सं खाली क देलखिन्ह, किएक त खुदाई के उपकरण बाढ़ि सं भरल गाम मे खुदाई करय लेल गाड़ी सं घुसि गेल छल.

नेपाल के नुवाकोट जिला में आकस्मिक बाढ़ के बाद चारि दिन के अंतराल के बाद शनिदिन घर वापसी के बाद शोबा श्रेष्ठ अपन कुत्ता स्वीटी के पानि दैत छथि। (दार यासिन/द एसोसिएटेड प्रेस)

परिवारक आशा खत्म होबय लगैत अछि

नेपालक राजधानी काठमांडूमे भोरेसँ सुबहसँ सम्बन्धी आ मित्र सभ मुख्य सरकारी अस्पतालक बाहर जमा भेल छल, लापता प्रियजनके समाचारक खोजमे बेताब भऽ गेल छल ।

बहुतो गोटे हेल्प डेस्क आ अस्पतालक नोटिस बोर्डक बीच घुमा-फिरा क' फोटो पकड़ि लेलक आ घायल मरीजक सूची स्कैन क' रहल छल, एहि आशा मे जे ओकरा भेटि जायत.

दिल माया लामा अस्पताल मे हेल्प डेस्क क बाहर कानि-कानि कए ठाढ़ भ अपन लापता 26 वर्षीय भाई, जे रसुवा क एकटा जलविद्युत कंपनी क ड्राइवर अछि, क जानकारी ताकि रहल छलीह। करीब 130 किलोमीटर दूर रामेछाप स यात्रा केने छलीह।

ओ कहलीह जे हम एहि उम्मीद स एतय आयल छलहुं जे कहीं हुनका भेटि जाएत। "हुनकर कोनो जानकारी नहि अछि।"

अस्पताल हेल्प डेस्क के सुरक्षा अधिकारी गजेन्द्र रावत कहलनि जे, आपदा के बाद सं एखन धरि परिवार करीब 1600 लापता लोक के पंजीकृत क चुकल अछि। ओ कहलनि जे, नेपाल के सब भाग स लोक आबि रहल अछि।

वापस नुवाकोट में सैन्य कर्मी सब एकटा राहत केंद्र के देबाल पर दर्जनों लापता लोक के सूचीबद्ध कागज के चादर के टेप क देलक, जाहि सं परिवार के आसपास भीड़ लागि गेल. किछु गोटे लापता आ मृतकक सूची स्कैन केलनि, फोटो खिंचौलनि आ नाम देखैत नोर पोछि लेलनि।

"हमरा आशा अछि, संयोगवश, जे हमर बेटा कतहु अछि" - ओ बजैत काल कानैत बाजल। "शायद ओ सभ ओकरा कतहु फँसल पाबि लेत। हम मात्र ओहि क्षणक प्रतीक्षा क' रहल छी।"

नेपाली सेना प्रवक्ता ब्रिगेडियर जनरल एस. राजा राम बस्नेट नँ कहलकै कि जलविद्युत निर्माण स्थल प बचाव के प्रयास जारी रहतै, जहां अधिकारियौ के मानना ​​छै कि सौ सँ अधिक लोग मोटऽ कीचड़ स॑ भरलऽ सुरंग म॑ फंसलऽ छै ।

बस्नेट कहलनि जे, बचावकर्मी किछु लोक तक पहुंचय लेल टोकरी आ रस्सी के इस्तेमाल केने छल, मुदा ऑपरेशन मुश्किल बनल अछि।

नेपाल के राजधानी काठमांडू में शुक्रदिन एकटा अस्पताल के बाहर प्रदर्शित आकस्मिक बाढ़ि में मृतक के फोटो देखय लेल लोक के भीड़ लागल अछि, जाहि सं रिश्तेदार के पीड़ित के पहचान करय में मदद मिलत. (दार यासिन/द एसोसिएटेड प्रेस)

हुनी कहलकै कि जबे अधिकारियौ नँ संभावित आरू बाढ़ के बारे मँ चेतावनी जारी करलकै तबे बचाव टीम क भी अस्थायी तौर प स्थानांतरित करै ल॑ मजबूर होय गेलऽ छै ।

बुधदिन शुरुआती बाढ़ि के बाद हिमालयी पहाड़ के ऊँचाई पर बनल नव झील सं आओर बाढ़ि के लेल बचावकर्मी हाई अलर्ट पर अछि. विशेषज्ञ सब चेतावनी देलनि जे ग्लेशियर के ढहला के बाद बनल एहि झील में बाढ़ि के उफान शुरू भ गेल अछि।

चीन के जल संसाधन मंत्रालय के निगरानी के आंकड़ा शुक्रदिन देर राति सं पता चलल जे झील के आकार कम भ गेल अछि. चीनी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी जनौलक अछि जे बृहस्पतिदिन भोर मे जलस्तर उच्च बिन्दु सँ १० मीटर घटल अछि ।

नेपालक राजधानी काठमांडू सँ प्रभावित क्षेत्र दिस सहायता ट्रक जा रहल देखल जा सकैत छल ।

कनाडा के विदेश मंत्री अनिता आनंद शनिदिन सोशल मीडिया पर कहलनि जे, पहिने लापता एकटा कनाडाई सुरक्षित भेटल अछि।

आनंद नँ कहलकै कि अभी भी ३१ कनाडाई के हिसाब नै छै, आरू ई बात के ध्यान रखतें हुअय कि जानकारी उपलब्ध होय के साथ-साथ ई आंकड़ा मँ अखनी भी “उतार-चढ़ाव” आबी सकै छै ।

तबाह चीन-नेपाल सीमा पर खोज जारी अछि

चीनी प्रसारक नेपालक संग कड़ा प्रभावित सीमा क्रासिंग ग्यिरॉंग बन्दरगाह पर पहुँचल बचावकर्मीक तस्वीर शनिदिन देखौलक। कियो पैदल या बेड़ा के माध्यम सं एहि इलाका मे पहुंचल छल, त कियो एहि इलाका मे उड़ाओल गेल ड्रोन सं नीचा उतरि गेल छल. "कियो, कियो?" बचावकर्मी चिचिया उठल।

बाढ़ि के समय सीमा नाका भवन मे कतेक लोक छल से तत्काल पता नहि चलल।

सिन्हुआ न्यूज एजेंसी द्वारा जारी ई फोटो म॑ ड्रोन माल ढुलाई करी रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि शनिदिन ग्योरॉंग काउंटी केरऽ कीचड़ स॑ प्रभावित इलाका म॑ खोज-बचाव अभियान चलैलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । (जियांग फैन/सिन्हुआ/द एसोसिएटेड प्रेस)

शनिदिन नेपालक आपदा एजेन्सी जनौलक अछि जे मृतकक संख्या ६२६ भऽ गेल अछि, जाहिमे देशमे २४२६ गोटे लापता अछि । नेपालमे एखन धरि ३७०० सँ बेसी लोकके उद्धार भेल अछि ।

चीन म॑ शुक्रवार क॑ मृतकऽ के संख्या सात होय गेलै, कैन्हेंकि सरकारी मीडिया न॑ गाँवऽ क॑ खाली करै के काम आरू नेता सिनी के राहत प्रतिक्रिया क॑ निर्देशित करै के कोशिश देखैलकै । चीन के सरकारी मीडिया के कहनाय छनि जे चीनी पक्ष सं 554 लोक लापता अछि. सैकड़ों लापता विदेशी छथि जे एहि इलाका मे काज करय लेल, ट्रेकिंग करय लेल या कोनो पवित्र चोटी के तीर्थ यात्रा करय लेल आयल छलाह.

title: Hawaii Nepalese community reacts to deadly flooding in Nepal - Hawaii News Now
description: Hawaii Nepalese community reacts to deadly flooding in Nepal  Hawaii News Now
publisher.title: Hawaii News Now
full_article:
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - Hawaii’s Nepalese community is closely monitoring catastrophic flooding in Nepal.

More than 600 people are confirmed dead after flooding near the China border, while about 2,500 people, including Americans and other foreign nationals, remain missing.

Experts believe the disaster may have been caused by a glacier collapse.

Dinesh Timilsina, president of the Society of Nepalese in Hawaii, said the tragedy is hitting the local community hard.

“So this tragedy feels very personal,” Timilsina said. “Right now I think the community focuses on rescue and finding those who are still missing and making sure the survivors have plenty of food, shelter and basic necessities.”

He called it a difficult and emotional time for the community.

The Society of Nepalese in Hawaii said it is continuing to monitor the situation and plans to share ways the community can support relief efforts in Nepal.

title: Nepal flood death toll nears 700, with more than 3,000 missing, as poor weather hampers rescues - CBS News
description: Nepal flood death toll nears 700, with more than 3,000 missing, as poor weather hampers rescues  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
The death toll from Wednesday's devastating flash floods in Nepal and along the border with China has risen to nearly 700, with around 3,000 people still missing, as rescue operations entered their fourth day.

The combined toll in Nepal and Tibet, an autonomous region in China, rose to 691 dead and over 3,000 people missing after China's latest update on Sunday.

Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing, while Nepal's disaster agency said late Saturday that the death toll had climbed to 675 with 2,498 people missing.

Poor weather and challenging terrain have hampered aerial rescue operations.

In Nuwakot, one of the Nepali districts devastated by the floods, helicopters resumed operations before noon Saturday after poor weather temporarily obstructed their activities. Some helicopters were loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice. Others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors.

An aerial view shows debris and mud covering settlements following flash floods on Aug. 28, 2026, in DevGhat village, Nepal. Ritesh Shukla / Getty Images

Families of the missing have been waiting for news of loved ones outside an army camp near Nuwakot.

A Nepali Army official told CBS News that its search and rescue helicopters could do a combined 15 trips an hour back and forth into the disaster zone, for a total of about 500 trips per day. Each flight is bringing in a handful of people, some carried out by stretcher.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far, according to authorities there. Hundreds of the missing are foreigners who were in the area to work, trek or make a pilgrimage to a sacred peak on the Tibet side of the border.

Amid the frantic search for survivors, Nepal issued a warned Sunday morning local time of further rising flood waters.

"We have received information that the flood flow in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa has increased further," the country's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said in an alert obtained by Agence France-Presse.

"Therefore, all personnel engaged in search, rescue, and relief operations, those in riverside areas, and everyone else in affected areas including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, and Chitwan are requested to exercise caution."

The U.S. State Department, meanwhile, said in a social media post Saturday that it was providing more than $3.6 million in humanitarian aid to Nepal, which would include three months of emergency food assistance designed to help up to 10,000 households.

Authorities search for dozens trapped in tunnels

Nepal's government says more than 100 workers may still be alive and trapped inside tunnels at hydropower projects, with rescue efforts focused on the Trishuli 3A and 3B sites. Initial reports suggested the 100 trapped were in a single location, but Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said "rescue efforts are going on in multiple tunnel sites." Rescuers managed to reach some people with helicopter baskets and ropes, but struggled with 4 to 5 feet of mud and limited landing sites, Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said.

On Saturday, rescuers broke through the mud at Trishuli 3A. They were able to begin sending air into the tunnel, and excavation efforts are underway, Nepali Home Minister Sudan Gurung. The Ministry of Energy reported efforts to send a camera into the tunnel have begun.

Specialized Indian and Chinese tunnel-rescue teams have joined the effort to free the trapped workers. India has extensive experience with difficult Himalayan tunnel rescues, including teams of "rat-hole" miners skilled in being able to crawl into narrow spaces. Nepal's expert mountain rescue teams — used to aiding climbers on the world's highest peaks, including Everest — are also joining the search for the missing.

Photographs shared by Nepal's disaster office showed workers wading through churned mud and navigating vast boulders left by the floods.

Priti Kharel said she believes her brother Milan is one of those trapped. He works as an engineering geologist at Doosan Enerbility, and his family has not heard from him since the floods. Kharel said friends who were at the site told her family that Milan might still be there.

"It's already four days," Kharel said. "We want the government to rescue him as soon as possible."

A woman walks through mud and debris left behind by flash flooding in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh) Rajesh Kumar Singh

Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said locating those still missing is "currently our national priority." He said Nepal's government has sought specialized support from neighbors for tunnel rescue, survivor-detection technology, rapid forensic and DNA analysis, and morgue refrigerators.

Khanal said an 11-member tunnel rescue reconnaissance team from India has been deployed, while a similar rescue team from China is expected shortly, he added.

Families search for information

At relief centers, families are waiting anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of those missing continue to rise. Others scour hospitals and paper lists for any signs of hope.

In Kathmandu, Nepal's capital, relatives and friends gathered outside the main government hospital from early morning, desperately searching for news of missing loved ones. Many shuffled between the help desk and the hospital notice board, clutching photographs and scanning injured patients' lists in the hope of finding them.

Families covered hospital walls with posters showing missing relatives, photographs and contact numbers in a desperate appeal for any clue that could bring them home. Nearby were photographs of unidentified bodies that officials put up in hopes families or friends could recognize them.

Gajendra Rawat, a security official at the hospital help desk, said families had so far registered around 1,600 missing persons since the disaster struck.

"People are coming from all parts of Nepal," he said.

Residents carry their belongings salvaged from their damaged homes filled with mud and debris in Devighat, in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026, following the Aug. 26 flash floods. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh) Rajesh Kumar Singh

Dil Maya Lama stood weeping outside the help desk at the hospital, searching for information about her missing 26-year-old brother, a driver for a hydropower company in Rasuwa. She had traveled from Ramechhap, about 80 miles away.

"I came here with the hope that I might find him," she said. "There is no information about him."

Nelza Moktan anxiously sought information about her missing cousin, who also worked as a driver in Rasuwa.

"I feel hopeless. It has already been four days," she said.

Back in Nuwakot, military personnel taped sheets of paper listing dozens of missing people to a wall at a relief center, prompting families to crowd around them. Some scanned lists of the missing and dead, took photos and wiped away tears. Rajesh Kumar Ram, who is searching for his son, desperately searched a list for his son's name.

"I'm hopeful, by chance, that my son is somewhere," he said, crying as he spoke. "Maybe they find him stuck somewhere. I'm waiting for that moment only."

The Red Cross said Friday that some 90,000 people had likely been impacted by the flooding. Khanal said Nepal has received over 57 metric tons of relief supplies from India, with additional aid arriving from China, Japan, Australia and other countries. Khanal added that further support will be sought as needs assessments continue.

In this photo released by Xinhua News Agency, rescuers carry out search and rescue operations at the mudslide-hit area in Gyirong County, southwest China's Tibet Autonomous Region on Saturday, Aug. 29, 2026. (Zheng Lijun/Xinhua via AP) Zheng Lijun

Authorities wary of further flood risk

Rescuers have been on high alert for more flooding from a new lake that formed high up in the Himalayan mountains after the initial floods on Wednesday. Experts warned that the lake, created after the glacier collapse that triggered the floods, was starting to overflow.

Basnet said rescue teams had been forced to relocate temporarily when authorities issued warnings about possible further flooding.

Monitoring data from the Chinese Ministry of Water Resources showed late Friday that the lake had dwindled in size. The water level dropped by 32 feet from its high point on Thursday morning, Chinese broadcaster CCTV said.

Scientists said satellite images indicated that the initial flooding was caused when bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event. The rocks and melted water suddenly swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing torrents of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria who is currently based in Bangladesh, said "a lower part of a glacier has really come off."

Satellite images show a valley of the Langtang Lirung mountain peak in Nepal on June 25, 2026, and Aug. 26, 2026, when devastating flooding struck the country. Sabrina Blanchard and Luca Matteucci/AFP via Getty Images

The Hindu Kush Himalayan region is warming rapidly , driving major changes in glaciers, snow cover, permafrost and mountain slopes, according to climate scientists. Around 78% of the glacier area, located between about 14,760 and 19,685 feet above sea level, is highly exposed to warming.

"What happened yesterday is unfortunately the new normal. It's going to get worse from here onwards," Steiner said.

Khanal said in a statement obtained by AFP that he spoke by phone his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, and both agreed to increase the sharing of "real-time hydrological data."

Wang, in a Chinese foreign ministry statement obtained by AFP, said Beijing had "shared crucial information with Nepal, including disaster area imagery, satellite and hydrological data, as well as early warnings about upstream barrier lakes."

Wang added that "China and Nepal are bound by mountains and rivers, sharing a common destiny."

Khanal earlier told reporters that Nepal needed greater research to "understand the changing dynamics of the Himalayan ecosystem," and the risks they pose to the landlocked country, encircled by India and China, AFP reported.

Americans among the missing

Five Americans have made their way to safety, and around 90 are among those unaccounted for, the U.S. State Department said Friday.

In a statement, the U.S. Embassy in Nepal said the U.S. was "delivering a range of supplies requested by the Government of Nepal and is working with Nepal to ensure that assistance reaches the people who need it."

"Catholic Relief Services, working through implementing partner Caritas Nepal, will deliver more than 2.5 metric tons of food supplies, 500 blankets, 500 mosquito nets, and 500 insulating foam sheets for temporary shelter flooring to two school locations in Rasuwa," the embassy said, noting plans for subsequent supply shipments were already in place.

Twenty-two people from the U.S. were among the 80 who went missing from a pilgrimage run by the Isha Foundation, a volunteer-run group that promotes well-being founded by Indian spiritual leader Sadhguru Vasudev.

"At this point we are awaiting word," community liaison Leslie Crespi said in a phone interview from McMinnville, Tennessee, of the missing pilgrims. "We have done as much outreach as we can through the State Department, through the embassy."

The 22 missing Americans were all adults, and included 13 women and nine men, the foundation later said in data it provided to CBS News. She said the Isha Foundation has organized pilgrimages for 21 years, and "in those 21 years, we have never lost a life."

U.S. citizen Deepak Dandu said his wife, Sridevi Vejella, was among those missing in Nepal. She was on the pilgrimage with the Isha Foundation to Mount Kailash in Tibet — a sacred site for Hindus, Buddhists and others — which he said was a "lifelong dream" for her.

Extensive destruction and debris deposits along the Trishuli River corridor following a catastrophic outburst flood and debris flow in Bidur, Nuwakot district, Nepal, on Aug. 28, 2026. Sameer Shrestha/Anadolu via Getty Images

He told CBS News she was crossing from China into Nepal when the flood hit. The foundation told him she was part of a group that was present at the Gyirong Port immigration complex.

President Trump called the flooding terrible to see on Thursday, saying that "strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks."

He told reporters in the Oval Office that U.S. officials had spoken with Nepalese leaders and offered to provide "anything they want."

Ramy Inocencio contributed to this report.
